The bug summary says an option '-mindirect-branch-register' is not handled correctly in combination with '-fno-plt'. Common target configuration is a strong Stage1 candidate because target-common code often normalizes, validates, and propagates target option state before backend expansion; mishandling of an x86 target option interaction can originate here.

This is fundamentally an option-interaction bug involving -mindirect-branch-register and -fno-plt. The options module is responsible for language-independent option definition, decoding, aliases, and compiler-side option state management, making it relevant for whether the combined flags are recorded and exposed correctly to later target code.

The reproducer checks final call/jump asm forms such as direct 'call/jmp bar' versus indirect through GOT/register under -fno-plt. ranked_methods.reason: This is the strongest match to the bug’s observable behavior. Its body directly decides between direct call/jmp emission and the -fno-plt GOT-based form, and then further routes non-direct calls/jumps through ix86_output_indirect_branch when indirect_branch_type != indirect_branch_keep. That is exactly the problematic interaction: with -fno-plt, calls stop being direct, and with -mindirect-branch-register they should be emitted via register-indirect branch sequences. The function also explicitly handles both normal calls and sibling calls, matching the tests that distinguish call vs jmp.

This small helper is central because it is the predicate that turns a direct symbol call into the special no-pic/no-plt path. It returns true specifically when !flag_plt or a noplt attribute applies, excluding local symbols and several target modes. Since the bug is precisely about -fno-plt interaction, this predicate is a key upstream gate feeding ix86_output_call_insn’s alternate GOT/indirect emission path.

ranked_methods.reason: This is the most direct implementation of the '-mindirect-branch-register' side of the bug. Its body emits indirect calls/jumps via registers or thunks depending on cfun->machine->indirect_branch_type, including separate sibcall and non-sibcall handling. Once -fno-plt causes GOT-based indirect calls, this routine is part of the exact machinery expected to convert those into register-based indirect branches.

This function materializes per-function indirect branch policy into cfun->machine->indirect_branch_type from attributes or the global ix86_indirect_branch setting. Since ix86_output_call_insn checks cfun->machine->indirect_branch_type != indirect_branch_keep to decide whether to route through indirect-branch emission, this function is a critical upstream state setter for whether -mindirect-branch-register actually influences call/jump output.

This is the bridge that installs function-specific target state before code generation. It explicitly calls ix86_set_indirect_branch_type for each function and restores the effective target option node. For an option interaction bug, especially one involving function-specific codegen state consulted during asm output, this body is highly relevant because it determines whether the backend sees the intended indirect-branch policy at emission time.

Although small, this function embodies the backend’s PLT-vs-non-PLT decision for symbol calls, returning false for local symbols and true otherwise except ifunc special cases. The issue summary is specifically about handling of -fno-plt, so any place deciding whether a call should use the PLT remains highly suspicious. It is slightly below ix86_nopic_noplt_attribute_p because the latter is explicitly referenced inside the actual output path shown in ix86_output_call_insn.
